A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RAGDiffusion and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across renaming, renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original STGarment experiments, component ablations, retrieval analyses, a user study and supplementary generalization demonstrations.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds cross-dataset evaluations, additional comparisons, mask-prediction experiments, manipulation examples and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V2 adds an optional inference procedure in supplementary Section 6.2: users replace the recommended landmark with another retrieved candidate before denoising. The core StructureNet, SLLE, EP-Adapter, ReferenceNet and PGEA pipeline remains. The Resampler label replacing MLP in Figure 2 clarifies an architecture already documented in v1's appendix.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on Viton-HD and DressCode, including upper-body, lower-body and dress subsets, plus extreme-garment and user-controlled shape scenarios. V1's pose-control, finger-refinement and background-replacement demonstrations are removed. The 856-item retrieval expansion and 50-query lower-body/dress study already existed in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: STGarment Table 1 expands from PBE, IP-Adapter and ReferenceNet to also include ControlNet, TryOffDiff and TryOffAnyone. Figure 3 replaces the IP-Adapter/PBE columns with the two garment-restoration methods, and Figure 4 adds TryOffAnyone. IGR is discussed but is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds DISTS to the evaluation metrics, changes the reported user-study population from 25 to 100 participants while retaining 200 image pairs, and revises StructureNet pretraining from nearly 200 million to 2 million images. New cross-dataset testing distinguishes zero-shot evaluations from Viton-HD-trained checkpoints. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct UNet mask-prediction alternative to test the necessity of retrieval, extreme-shape/pattern robustness examples, landmark-manipulation case studies and cross-dataset generalization analysis. Existing embedding, retrieval-size, nearest-neighbor sensitivity and color-failure analyses remain. V1's generic training-free RAG demonstrations are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions describe user-score distributions through means, medians, quartiles and outliers. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The changed participant count and plotted scores alter study settings and results, without changing the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline/DISTS scores, cross-dataset results, mask-prediction results and runtime measurements. For example, Table 3 reports a DressCode-lower FID of 40.5, and Table 2 gives mask prediction an FID of 14.55. The original STGarment RAGDiffusion FID remains 9.990. Figure 4 changes its annotated RAGDiffusion scores from 8.34/8.52 to 8.30/8.86, although v2's prose retains the old values; the participant setting also changed.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Equation 1 by adding the negative sign to the contrastive loss. Supplementary Equation 7 restores multiplication by V_text in the attention formula, omitted in v1. SLLE's assumptions and mathematical construction otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2's introduction adds human-interpretable landmark control as a benefit and foregrounds the zero-shot generalization claim previously developed in the appendix. The central contribution—retrieving external structural knowledge to improve garment fidelity—remains. The change from three-level alignment to coarse-to-fine texture alignment largely reorganizes existing components.

C2.justification: V2 expands the practical interpretation through explanations of direct-mask prediction failure, negligible retrieval overhead, user control and commercial logo fidelity. It acknowledges remaining failures on extreme shapes but removes v1's limitation concerning non-end-to-end training and its expertise/coding demands. These changes substantially revise the discussion of applicability and limitations; color-bias limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents FAISS-based parallel retrieval, a retrieval/denoising/captioning timing breakdown, and the raw-image conditioning used for ControlNet. Reported training and annotation hardware changes from A100 to H20 GPUs. Most existing architectural details, hyperparameters, dataset preprocessing and augmentation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion replaces generic image/document restoration with garment restoration, positioning RAGDiffusion against TileGAN, TryOffDiff, TryOffAnyone and IGR. It develops distinctions involving structural errors, commercial detail fidelity and adaptation costs. Additional references support the new metrics, retrieval implementation and benchmark coverage.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are substantially rewritten around garment restoration. Structure conditioning moves into Section 3.2, ablations are presented as cumulative component additions, and generalization is promoted into the main experiments. The supplementary rationale is reorganized, and references move after the supplementary material.

P2.justification: V2 expands comparison and ablation tables, adds cross-dataset and timing tables, changes comparison panels and the user-study display, and adds manipulation and extreme-garment figures. The sensitivity and t-SNE plots are merged, existing lower-body examples are partly redisplayed in the main text, and the generic RAG demonstration figure is removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited empirical validation by adding garment-restoration competitors, quantitative cross-dataset evaluation and a direct mask-prediction control. These additions test the value and generalizability of retrieval more directly than v1's generic baselines and qualitative transfer examples. Mathematical corrections and implementation disclosures also improve clarity. These gains outweigh the new Figure 4/prose inconsistency and the removal of the multistage-training limitation, although those issues weaken reporting consistency and qualification of practical claims.
